142. Application of Part IX
This Part does not apply to or in relation to–
consultants, advisers or agents (without executive authority or power of direction of members of a State Service) who are–
employed on an honorary basis: or
remunerated by fees or commission only, with or without travelling or subsistence allowances, expense allowances or similar allowances; or
except as provided by or under an Act of Parliament–
the holders of offices listed in section 165 (application of Division 5); or
the members of the staff of statutory authorities; or
members of, or members of the staff of, local governments or authorities.
Nothing in this Part prevents the creation of–
statutory offices; or
statutory corporations or authorities; or
statutory or administrative commissions, boards or committees, or similar bodies,
or the determination, in accordance with law, of conditions of employment relating to them.

143. The State Services
Subject to this Part, Acts of Parliament shall make provision for and in relation to–
a Public Service; and
the Tuvalu Police.
Subject to this Part, Acts of Parliament may make provision for and in relation to–
a Prison Service; and
other State Services of Tuvalu.
144. Creation etc, of offices, etc, in State Services

Subject to any Act of Parliament, the Cabinet may–
create or abolish offices or positions in State Services; and
determine the qualifications for offices or positions in State Services; and
prescribe the functions of offices or positions in State Services.

145. Appointments subject to approval, etc.
Except as provided in this Constitution, this section does not apply to or in relation to any office or position established by this Constitution.
Nothing in this Part prevents an appointment to, or other service action in relation to, an office or position in a State Service from being made subject to–
approval by Parliament, or by any other person or authority; or
consultation with Parliament or with the members of Parliament, or with any other person or authority.

146. Localization
In this section–
A localization policy or programme may be laid down–
by or under an Act of Parliament; or
by decision of the Cabinet, approved by Parliament by resolution.
Nothing in a policy or programme laid down in accordance with subsection (2)(b) affects any right to termination or retirement benefits, or to compensation, otherwise possessed by any person affected by it.
Nothing in this Part, including Division 5 (Removal, etc., of Certain Officials), or in Part II (Bill of Rights) prevents the implementation of any localization policy or programme laid down under this section.

"localization" means preference in public employment (either generally or in respect of an office or position, or a class of offices or positions) for–
citizens of Tuvalu; or
persons whose usual places of residence (apart from the requirements of employment) are in Tuvalu; or
persons having some other special connection with Tuvalu,
including the replacement of the holders of offices or positions who do not have the qualifications required by the policy.
A Public Service Commission is established.
The Public Service Commission shall consist of a Chairman and three other members.

149. Appointment of members of the Commission
The members of the Public Service Commission shall be appointed by the Head of State, acting in accordance with the advice of the Cabinet.
A person is not qualified for appointment as a member of the Commission if–
he is a member of Parliament; or
he is a candidate for election as a member of Parliament; or
he is the holder of–
any other office or position established by this Constitution; or
an office or position in a State Service; or
any other office or position prescribed for the purposes of this subsection by or under an Act of Parliament.

150. Remuneration, etc, of members of the Commission
The salary or other remuneration of the Chairman and the other members of the Public Service Commission are as provided for in section 173 (remuneration of certain officials).
The other conditions of employment of a member of the Commission are as prescribed by or under an Act of Parliament.

151. Tenure of office of members of the Commission
A member of the Public Service Commission vacates his office or position–
if he is removed from office under Division 5 (Removal etc., of certain officials); or
subject to subsection (2), if he resigns by notice in writing to the Head of State; or
if he ceases to be qualified for appointment by virtue of section 149(2) (which relates to disqualification from appointment); or
at the end of the period of four years after the date of his appointment.
A resignation under subsection (1)(b) takes effect on the date on which it is received by the Head of State, or on such later date as is fixed by agreement between the member and the Minister responsible for Public Service matters.

152. Exclusion of members of the Commission from certain employment
This section does not apply to a person who has been acting temporarily in the office of a member of the Public Service Commission only for a period of less than six consecutive months.
Nothing in this section prevents other or additional disqualifications being imposed by or under an Act of Parliament on–
a member or former member of the Public Service Commission, or
a person referred to in subsection (1), because of his membership or former membership of the Commission.
A member of the Public Service Commission is not eligible for appointment to any office or position referred to in section 149(2)(c) (which relates to certain offices and positions the holders of which are disqualified from appointment to the Public Service Commission).
DIVISION 3. GENERAL FUNCTIONS OF THE PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION

153. Functions of the Commission
Subject to this Constitution and in particular to section 154 (independence of the Commission), and to any Act of Parliament, the Public Service Commission is responsible for–
the efficient management and control of the Public Service in relation to matters referred to in paragraphs (a)-(f) of the definition "personnel matters" in section 141 (interpretation of Part IX);and
all personnel matters connected with the Public Service; and
such matters in relation to the other State Services and the services of other governmental bodies as are prescribed,
Subject to section 154 (independence of the Commission), the Public Service Commission–
may at any time; and
shall at the request of the Minister responsible for Public Service matters,
and has such other functions as are prescribed by the Constitution or an Act of Parliament
inform or advise the Cabinet as to any matter within the functions of the Commission.

154. Independence of the Commission
Subject to section 15 (independence) of Schedule 1, in personnel matters the Public Service Commission shall comply with any general directions as to policy given by the Cabinet, but otherwise is not subject to direction or control by any other person or authority.
A policy direction given under subsection (1)–
shall be published in any manner prescribed for the publication of subordinate legislation; and
shall immediately be forwarded by the Minister responsible for Public Service matters to the Speaker, for presentation to Parliament.
Except in relation to personnel matters, the Public Service Commission is responsible to the Cabinet for the performance of its functions.

155. Appeals within State Services
The independence conferred on the Public Service Commission by section 154 (independence of the Commission) is not affected by any provision of an Act of Parliament providing for an appeal, to an independent tribunal or authority established by an Act of Parliament, from–
a decision of the Commission; or
any recommendation or advice to the Commission; or
any advice proposed to be given by the Commission to the Head of State
The provisions of section 154 (independence of the Commission) and of subsection (1) apply to and in relation to any tribunal or authority that may be established under subsection (1) in the same way as they apply to and in relation to the Public Service Commission.
Subject to any Act of Parliament, the provisions of Schedule 3 (Procedures etc., of the Public Service Commission and Certain Tribunals) apply to and in respect of the Public Service Commission.

157. Delegation by the Commission
With the approval of the Minister responsible for Public Service matters, the Public Service Commission may, in writing, delegate to any person any of its functions.
A delegation under subsection (1)–
may apply generally, or in respect of any part of Tuvalu or of any place specified in the instrument of delegation; and
may be made subject to such conditions, limitations and restrictions as are so specified.
A delegation under this section is revocable, in writing, at will, and no delegation prevents the performance of a function by the Commission.
If a delegation under this section relates to personnel matters, in performing the delegated function the delegate is subject to the same freedom from direction or control as the Commission, and the provisions of sections 154 (independence of the Commission) and 155, (appeals within State Services) with the necessary modifications, apply accordingly.

158. Application of Division 4
This Division applies to and in relation to any Act of Parliament made for the purposes of section 143 (the State Services) establishing a State Service, and to any regulations or other subsidiary legislation made under such an Act.
The provisions of this Division shall be read subject to this Constitution and in particular to–
section 146 (Localization); and
Division 5 (Removal, etc., of Certain Officials).
Authority in relation to personnel matters in respect of members of the Public Service shall be vested in the Public Service Commission.

160. Magistrates
The provisions of this section apply in relation to a magistrate of a subordinate court irrespective of whether he is a member of the Public Service.
Authority in relation to personnel matters in respect of magistrates of subordinate courts in their capacity as magistrates shall be vested in the Head of State, acting in accordance with the advice of the Public Service Commission, subject to the approval, either general or specific, of the Chief Justice or a person authorised by him for the purpose.

161. The Police Service
An office of Commissioner of Police is established as an office in the Tuvalu Police.
The Commissioner of Police shall be appointed in accordance with section 163(5)(a) (which relates to the appointment of the Commissioner of Police).
Excluding the Commissioner of Police, members of the Tuvalu Police of or above the rank of Inspector (or the equivalent rank as defined by or under an Act of Parliament) maybe appointed, removed and disciplined in the same manner, with any necessary modifications, as members of the Public Service under section 159 (the Public Service).
Other members of the Tuvalu Police maybe appointed, removed and disciplined by the Commissioner of Police, subject to appeal to the Public Service Commission in the case of removal or disciplinary action.
The Director of Public Prosecution may initiate criminal proceedings against any Police Officer.

162. Office of Director of Public Prosecutions
The office of Director of Public Prosecutions is established as an office in the Public Service.
The Director of Public Prosecutions shall be appointed in accordance with section 163(6)(a) (which relates to the appointment of the Director of Public Prosecutions).
A person who is qualified to practise before the High Court is qualified to be appointed as the Director of Public Prosecutions.
The Director of Public Prosecutions in any case where he may consider it desirable to do so may–
institute and undertake criminal proceedings against any person before any court (other than a court-martial or other military tribunal) for any criminal offence; and
take over and continue any criminal proceedings that have been instituted or undertaken by any other person or authority; and
discontinue at any stage before judgement is delivered any criminal proceedings instituted or undertaken by the Director or any other person or authority.
The functions of the Director of Public Prosecutions under subsection (4) may, subject to an Act of Parliament, be exercised by the Director:
in person; or
through any other person acting under the Director‘s general or specific instructions, and any references to the Director include references to officers so acting.
The powers in subsection (4)(b) and (c) are vested in the Director to the exclusion of any other person or authority.
An Act of Parliament or any other law may provide other functions, duties or powers of the Director.
The Attorney-General shall exercise the powers of the Director if:
the office of the Director of Public Prosecutions becomes vacant; or
the Director is for any reason unable to perform the functions of the office.

shall be appointed by the Head of State, acting in accordance with the advice of the Public Service Commission, and with the approval of Parliament signified by resolution; and

shall be appointed by the Head of State, acting in accordance with the advice of the cabinet given after consultation with the Public Service Commission; and

shall be appointed by the Head of State acting in accordance with the advice of the Public Service Commission given after consultation with the Cabinet; and

shall be appointed by the Governor-General acting in his own deliberate judgement; and

166. Removal of prescribed officials from office
Subject to section 168 (contract employment), the holder of an office or position to which this Division applies may be removed from office only–
for inability to perform properly the functions of his office or position (whether arising from infirmity of body or mind, or from some other cause), or for misbehaviour; and
in accordance with this section.

the tribunal has advised the appropriate authority that he ought to be removed from office for a reason set out in subsection (1)(a).

167. Suspension of prescribed officials
If the question of removing a person from office has been referred to a tribunal under section 166 (removal of prescribed officials from office), the appropriate authority may suspend him from office.
A suspension under subsection (1)–
may be lifted at any time by the appropriate authority; and
ceases to have effect if the tribunal advises the appropriate authority that the person concerned should not be removed from office.

169. Parliamentary responsibility for finance
Notwithstanding anything in this Constitution (other than section 173 (remuneration of certain officials)), the raising and spending of money by the Government (including the imposition of taxation and the raising of loans) is subject to authorization and control by Parliament, and shall be regulated by an Act of Parliament.
For each financial year there shall be–
a National Budget, comprising estimates of–
money proposed to be raised by the Government; and
money proposed to be spent by the Government, in respect of the financial year; and
appropriations for the service of the financial year, and there may be such supplementary Budgets and supplementary appropriations as are necessary.

The person who immediately before the commencement date holds office as Governor-General under the Constitution of Tuvalu 1986 shall, as from that day, hold office as Governor-General as if he had been appointed thereto under section 56 (appointment, etc., of the Governor-General).
The person who holds office as Governor-General by virtue of subsection (1) shall be deemed to have complied with section 58 (oaths and affirmations by the Governor-General).
For the purpose of calculating the period of four years referred to in subsection (3)(e) of section 56 (appointment, etc., of the Governor-General) in relation to the person who holds office as Governor-General by virtue of subsection (1), that period shall be deemed to have commenced on the day of his appointment under the Constitution 1986, but without prejudice to the operation of any of the other provisions of subsection (3) of that section.
Subsection (3)(c) of section 56 (appointment etc., of the Governor-General) shall not apply in relation to the person who holds office as Governor-General by virtue of subsection (1).

Any person who immediately before the commencement date holds office as Prime Minister or any other Minister under the Constitution 1986 shall, as from that date, hold office as Prime Minister or other Minister, as the case may be, as if he had–
in the case of the Prime Minister, been elected thereto under section 64 (the Prime Minister); or
in the case of any other Minister, been appointed thereto under section 68 (the other Ministers).
Any person holding office as Prime Minister or other Minister by virtue of subsection (1) who before the commencement date was assigned, and immediately before that date held, responsibility for any business of the Government shall be deemed to have been assigned responsibility for that business under section 77 (assignment of responsibilities to Ministers).

Unless and until the number of members of Parliament is fixed pursuant to section 84 (composition of Parliament) by or under an Act of Parliament, the number of members is 16.
Any person who immediately before the commencement date is a member of the former Parliament shall on that day become a member of Parliament and shall be deemed to have complied with the requirements of section 115 (oath and affirmation of members of Parliament) and shall hold his seat in Parliament in accordance with the provisions of the Constitution.
The person who immediately before the commencement date holds the office of Speaker of the former Parliament shall on that day become Speaker of Parliament and shall hold office as such in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution.
The rules of procedure of the former Parliament as in force immediately before the commencement date shall, except as may be otherwise provided under section 110 (rules of procedure) have effect after that day as if they had been made under that section but shall be construed with such modifications, adaptions, qualifications and exceptions as may be necessary to bring them into conformity with this Constitution.
For the purpose of the first determination after the commencement date of the period of four years referred to in section 121(1) (which relates to the automatic dissolution of Parliament), that period shall be deemed to have commenced after the date of the first sitting of the former Parliament after the last general election preceding the commencement date.
Any Bill which, before the commencement date, was before the former Parliament–
shall not lapse; and
shall on and after the commencement date, be treated as a Bill for an Act before Parliament; and
may be proceeded with accordingly–
any stage of the Bill completed before the former Parliament being treated as having been completed before Parliament; and
any stage of the Bill commenced before the former Parliament being continued before Parliament.
Any business commenced before the former Parliament may, on and after the commencement date, be continued before Parliament.
In this section, "the former Parliament" means the Parliament of Tuvalu established by the Independence Constitution.

Every person who immediately before the commencement date holds or is acting in a public office shall, as from that day, hold or act in that office or the corresponding office established by this Constitution as if he had been appointed to do so in accordance with the provisions of this Constitution and shall be deemed to have taken any oaths required upon such appointment by any existing law.
Any person who holds office by virtue of subsection (1) and who would, under the Independence Constitution or any existing law, have been required to vacate office at the expiration of any period or on the attainment of any age shall vacate his office under this Constitution upon the expiration of that period or upon the attainment of that age.
The provisions of this section shall be without prejudice to any power conferred by or under this Constitution upon any person or authority to make provision for the abolition of offices and for the removal from office of persons holding or acting in any office.
In this section, "public office" shall be construed as including the office of member (including Chairman) of the Public Service Commission established by the Independence Constitution.

All proceedings commenced or pending before the commencement date before the High Court or the Court of Appeal of Tuvalu established by the Constitution 1986 may continue on and after that day before the High Court or the Court of Appeal Tuvalu, as the case may be, established by this Constitution.
Any decision given before the commencement date by the High Court or the Court of Appeal of Tuvalu established by the Constitution 1986 shall for the purposes of the enforcement or, in the case of a decision given by the High Court, for the purpose of any appeal therefrom, have effect on and after that day as if it were a decision of the High Court or the Court of Appeal of Tuvalu, as the case may be, established by this Constitution.

Any person who immediately before the commencement date holds office as a Judge under the Constitution of Tuvalu 1986 shall, as from that day, hold office as Judge as if he had been appointed thereto under sections 125 (the Chief Justice of Tuvalu) and 126 (other Judges) and shall hold office for 3 months.
The Judicial Services Commission shall endeavour to make new appointments within 3 months from the commencement date.
